findings: Canonical confined relative source paths reject traversal and symlink components; fixed unique identities/paths and exact SHA256 bind every persisted source.
Hydration requires externally expected ordered slot bindings, validates source contents again, recomputes domain summary and rejects rehashed summary tampering.
Lossless JSON roundtrip rejects invalid summary values; compact canonical serialization matches the existing stage writer representation.
Actual shared-stage test writes16 large source results then a reference final record under8KiB, successfully hydrates all payloads, and cleans test directories.
limitations: Helper alone does not enforce planned benchmark denominator, domain schema/usage, transport settlement or missing-slot placeholders; trusted wrapper must supply exact expected bindings and deterministic validator/summary.
Serialized-size cap is not a guarantee of physical filesystem allocation, entry availability or final reserve admission. The shared stage guard and final persistence remain mandatory.
Source files must be immutable and retained; hashes provide integrity rather than authorization.
Live wrapper/scorer integration and failure accounting remain unreviewed.
